items.title: 71542_Bill Coleman autobiographical manuscript
items.q: His name was Robert Burnier and we gave him the name of the 'Creep' because he was tall, skinny, wore a black overcoat and hat and seemed to be always creeping around a corner like Mack the Knife.

ctx.x: The 4th of February 1957 I left Paris for Italy to do a month's tour that featured Benny Waters on tenor and Albert Nicholas, clarinet Jack Starling, piano Gilbert Fanfant, bass and a German drummer, whom I can only remember his first name which was Rolfie. Cecily Forde was engaged as the singer. We did 21 concerts including two in Milano and played in every important city in Italy and some that were not.

The tour started the 8th of February. There were three booking agents handling this tour, two Italians and one Italo-American. One travelled with us. We were travelling by train. His name was Robert Burnier and we gave him the name of the "Creep" because he was tall, skinny, wore a black overcoat and hat and seemed to be always creeping around a corner like Mack the Knife.

During the tour we were engaged to play a big ball in St. Moritz, Switzerland, for the millionaire shipping magnate Niarkos, who was the brother in law of Onassis, another shipping magnate. The ball was given in the Palace Hotel which is the largest and most expensive hotel in that resort. And we also had rooms in that hotel.
